title: Just-in-Time Workstation Administration
built: Implemented native approval and a timed midPoint role that grants local administrator access through a dedicated AD group on one Windows workstation.
problem: Reduce standing administrator privileges while showing the difference between directory revocation and Windows session lifetime.
objective: Demonstrate denied access, temporary elevation, automatic group revocation and denial after fresh sign-in.
outcome: Verified the full denied → approved temporary access → automatic AD revocation → fresh-sign-in denial cycle. The role had a 15-minute validity window; membership removal was first observed 47.204 seconds after expiry. AD revocation left the Windows session active. A client restart was required to clear stale group information before the final online sign-in check. Native processing resumed after an application restart.
steps: Request and approve a timed assignment

limitations: Processing delay and previously issued Windows tokens prevent a precise 15-minute session cutoff. Full manual replay and outage across expiry were not tested.
overview_limitations: The 15-minute validity window is not a hard session cutoff. Scheduled processing adds delay, and Windows can retain stale groups across sign-out; the final client test required a restart. Full manual replay and an outage spanning expiry were not tested.
